ai-at-work.excerpt: The round valued the AI biotech at $2 billion. It is currently testing drugs that treat skin conditions and preserve weight loss after stopping GLP-1s.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Enveda just raised $311 million for AI-powered drug discovery focused on natural compounds, pushing their valuation to $2 billion while they test treatments for skin conditions and GLP-1 weight loss rebound. This matters because biotech AI adoption is accelerating across industries, and digital workplace teams supporting life sciences companies need to understand how their infrastructure supports complex collaborative research and regulatory compliance workflows. Here's the thing: while everyone's obsessing over ChatGPT writing emails, these companies are quietly using AI to decode nature and literally save lives, which is a good reminder that the real AI story isn't about chatbots.

ai-at-work.title: Even Americans who use AI every day are worried about it
ai-at-work.excerpt: The report suggests that greater exposure will not resolve the unease around the technology, nor reduce public support for AI regulation.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: A new report found that regular AI users in America remain anxious about the technology despite their daily exposure to it. This matters to digital workplace pros because it signals that rolling out AI tools to your workforce won't automatically build confidence or adoption, no matter how seamlessly you integrate them. The real lesson here is that throwing more AI at people won't fix their legitimate concerns, and pretending otherwise is how you end up with expensive tools nobody actually uses.

ai-at-work.title: Amazon’s new plugin lets sellers manage their entire e-commerce business with AI
ai-at-work.excerpt: Amazon.com Inc. said today it’s trying to make life easier for independent sellers using its ecommerce platform with new tools including a plugin that allows them to run their businesses via artificia
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Amazon rolled out AI-powered plugins that let independent sellers automate and manage their entire ecommerce operations through AI assistants. This matters because it shows how AI is moving into workflow automation at scale, which means digital workplace tools need to evolve fast to keep pace or risk looking like typewriters. Honestly, if your organization isn't already thinking about how AI assistants integrate with your core business processes, you're about to get lapped by companies that did this six months ago.

ai-at-work.title: Google launches two benchmark-topping speech generation models

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google released two new text-to-speech models, Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS, through its cloud platform with similar APIs that let developers swap between them easily. This matters because digital workplaces are increasingly embedding voice into everything from employee training to accessibility tools, and having cost-efficient options means more organizations can actually afford to implement decent audio features. Finally, we're getting somewhere on the cost side of AI, though I'll believe "benchmark-topping" means anything practical once I hear it handle a Scottish accent without turning it into a fever dream.

tools-tech.title: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill
tools-tech.excerpt: ZDNET Exclusive: A new Workera report shows businesses and employees aren’t on the same page about AI upskilling. Here’s what organizations need to know.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Two-thirds of workers are already using AI tools on the job, yet most companies aren't carving out time for people to actually learn how to use them properly. This is a real problem for digital workplace leaders because it means your workforce is flying blind, cobbling together knowledge from YouTube videos and lunch break Slack conversations instead of proper training. You've got people steering the plane while reading the manual, and honestly, that's exactly how you end up with data leaks, security nightmares, and a bunch of very frustrated employees wondering why nobody taught them anything.

tools-tech.title: AI spend will jump 49.5% in 2026, says Gartner
tools-tech.excerpt: Worldwide AI spending will increase 49.5% in 2026, to $2.7 trillion, and grow another 36.2% in 2027 as AI usage continues to expand, Gartner predicts in the latest quarterly update to its IT spending
tools-tech.dwp_take: Gartner is predicting global AI spending will hit $2.7 trillion in 2026, jumping nearly 50 percent year over year, with growth continuing strong into 2027. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because it signals that AI investments aren't cannibalizing other critical workplace tech budgets, meaning you might actually have resources for collaboration tools, security, and infrastructure alongside those shiny AI pilots. Here's the reality though: predictions are fun, but most organizations I work with are still figuring out how to get actual ROI from their first AI experiments instead of chasing the next forecast number.

tools-tech.title: OpenAI’s new priorities for third-party assessments are a fine start, but they lack teeth
tools-tech.excerpt: OpenAI published a detailed list of priorities and principles on Tuesday designed to govern its third-party model assessors, a list that industry observers agreed was a good one. But they also stresse
tools-tech.dwp_take: OpenAI released guidelines for third-party AI assessors that sound good on paper but have no enforcement mechanisms behind them. For digital workplace leaders evaluating AI tools for their organizations, this matters because vague principles without teeth make it harder to actually assess risk and compliance. Here's the thing: telling enterprise CIOs that safety is important while refusing to be audited is a bit like saying you're committed to security but won't let anyone check the locks.

tools-tech.title: From admin to architect: Jamf’s vision for the autonomous Apple enterprise

tools-tech.dwp_take: Jamf, now private, is rolling out AI-powered tools to help IT teams manage Apple device fleets at scale, with CEO Beth Tschida unveiling major platform changes at their JNUC conference. This matters because most enterprises are drowning in Apple devices they barely understand, so automation that actually works could free IT teams from the tedium of manual device management. Here's the thing though: I've seen plenty of "autonomous" promises from vendors over three decades, and the real question is whether Jamf's AI actually reduces ticket volume or just moves the headache around.

digital-culture.title: How to handle being blamed for something that isn’t your fault
digital-culture.excerpt: When something goes wrong at work, a good organization focuses on what caused the problem and what can be done to ensure it does not happen again. If someone has made a mistake, we expect them to own
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company published a piece on how to navigate blame when you're actually innocent, focusing on how healthy organizations investigate root causes instead of playing the blame game. This matters because digital workplace professionals are constantly caught between competing systems, platforms, and departments, making it easy for someone to finger IT when the real problem lives three layers upstream. Look, I have seen countless tickets labeled "email is broken" that were actually Outlook calendar sync issues, user misconfiguration, or even people not knowing how to check their spam folder, so if your workplace is still doing the blame dance instead of the root cause tango, you're wasting time and poisoning culture.

digital-culture.title: Most workers are working on Sundays—here’s why
digital-culture.excerpt: Nearly three-quarters of workers (74%) work on Sunday, including 21% who work a full or near-full day, according to Owl Labs’ tenth annual State of Hybrid Work report. The trend is far more common amo
digital-culture.dwp_take: Nearly three-quarters of workers now do at least some work on Sundays, with younger generations particularly prone to the habit, according to Owl Labs' latest hybrid work report. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand that "always on" culture isn't just a nice-to-have problem anymore, it's a retention and burnout risk that's baked into how we've designed remote work. Here's the thing: if your digital workplace infrastructure makes it frictionless to work on Sunday, people will, and then you get to explain to HR why everyone's exhausted by February.

digital-culture.title: 5 science-backed strategies to be a better boss

digital-culture.dwp_take: Caroline Webb, an executive coach and McKinsey advisor, distilled five science-backed management strategies from her new book on leadership intelligence. Digital workplace leaders need to know this stuff because remote and hybrid teams require managers who actually understand human behavior instead of just barking orders through Slack. Look, after three decades watching workplace tech implementations fail because leadership stayed stuck in 1987, I can tell you that behavioral science beats buzzwords every single time.

digital-culture.title: How to tell if people who look good in meetings are just faking it
digital-culture.excerpt: Whether you work remotely or in an office (or a mix of both), meetings are an integral part of work, especially for knowledge workers. According to recent estimates, the average American professional
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece is exploring how to spot people who appear competent in meetings but might actually be phoning it in. This matters because we've all been duped by someone who nods confidently while contributing nothing, and if you can't read the room accurately, you're making hiring and promotion decisions on performance theater. The real skill isn't looking good in meetings—it's recognizing that most of us are just trying to survive 14 years of our lives trapped in them.

industry-news.title: OpenAI Expands Outside Safety Reviews Into Model Training
industry-news.excerpt: OpenAI plans to expand independent safety assessments into model training and evaluation, giving outside groups earlier access to test high-risk AI systems. The post OpenAI Expands Outside Safety Revi
industry-news.dwp_take: OpenAI is letting independent safety researchers peek under the hood during model development instead of waiting until after release. This matters because digital workplace tools powered by AI are rolling out faster than ever, and having external eyes on safety earlier means fewer surprises when these systems hit your company's servers. Here's the thing though: good intentions are nice, but "we're getting better at this" only counts if the outside reviewers actually have teeth and aren't just rubber-stamping whatever OpenAI wants to ship.

industry-news.dwp_take: Beats released $350 headphones with swappable cushions, 32-hour battery life, and improved noise cancellation across both Apple and Android platforms.
